plans.note: Section 7 is captioned 'Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor' — review the cap for mutuality, a meaningful amount tied to fees paid, and carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, gross negligence/willful misconduct). Heading suggests a one-sided, Contractor-favourable construct.

Section 7 provides indemnification of Contractor only; a Vendor-side indemnity for third-party IP claims and Contractor misconduct appears absent. Add vendor indemnity and narrow any Clear Capital indemnity in sec-7.
No restrictive-covenant section in the outline; scan sec-1 (Purpose of Engagement) and sec-6 for any limits on our business activities or competing purchases before concluding absence.
No exclusivity provision visible; sec-1 scope and sec-3 compensation are the only plausible homes for an exclusive-engagement or sole-source undertaking.
Pricing sits in sec-3; check for any obligation on us to extend RadialSpark best terms. An MFN in our favour would be acceptable, so confirm direction before flagging.

No non-solicit section appears in the outline; contractor engagements often bury a hiring restriction in the personnel or termination text (sec-1, sec-6) — verify, and require a general-advertising carve-out if present.

Section 6 (Termination) is the operative clause: confirm we hold termination for convenience on short notice with no penalty or acceleration, and that Contractor cannot terminate at will mid-engagement.
Term and renewal mechanics likely sit in sec-6 or in the unlisted Section 2; check for auto-renewal, notice window length and any uncapped renewal price increase.

No general/miscellaneous section is listed, so governing law and venue may be missing or held in an unlisted tail section; if absent, add New York (or DE/CA/E&W) law with court jurisdiction and no foreign arbitration.
No assignment clause in the outline; if it does not exist, add affiliate/successor assignment rights for us and remove any Contractor termination or consent trigger on our change of control.

Section 4 (Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance) is the primary target: confirm work product and deliverables vest in Clear Capital, that our data and pre-existing IP are untouched, and that any Contractor retained-rights language is limited to generic tools.
Any licence-back or residual licence for Contractor background IP will sit in sec-4; ensure the grant to us extends to affiliates and contractors and is irrevocable, not revocable at will.
No audit clause appears; check sec-3 (records/invoicing) and sec-4 for any inspection right against us — if present, require notice, frequency limits, off-site review and Contractor-borne cost.
Watch sec-3 for late-payment penalties or termination fees and sec-6 for early-termination charges; liquidated damages payable by us should be struck, while credits in our favour are fine.

Section 5 carries the representations plus a warranty disclaimer — confirm a performance warranty of meaningful duration against the Specifications with re-performance/refund remedy, and resist a broad 'AS IS' disclaimer; sec-4 acceptance testing supports the remedy.
No insurance section in the outline; add standard coverages (CGL, professional liability/E&O, cyber, workers' comp) near sec-5 given Contractor personnel and possible data access.
Review sec-3 (Contractor's Compensation) for minimum hours, retainers or take-or-pay commitments; if present, tie them to our termination right in sec-6 so there is a clean exit.
Section 6 likely addresses only wind-down of fees; add post-termination transition assistance and return/deletion of our data and materials, coordinated with the ownership provisions in sec-4.
